chapter_approach.heading: How this chapter is taught
chapter_approach.intro: The chapter opens with a story about a toy box. You try the toys yourself before any shape has a name. Then a story gives each idea its name, and a tool lets you try it. The questions from your maths book come on that tool. A short look back ends the chapter.

points.title: Try first, name later
points.text: You push, turn and stand real toys before you learn a shape name. Then a story gives each solid its name, so the name has something to hold on to.

points.title: Real objects, plain solids
points.text: A football, a die, a shoebox, a bottle and a birthday cap stand for the five solids. A sphere is always a solid ball and never a flat circle.

points.title: Your maths book questions sit on the tools
points.text: Each question comes on the tool for its idea. Things you do with real objects, such as craft, building, cubes and the dice game, are on the screen too.

points.title: Answers marked as they are

tool_config.title: Explore Shapes Around Us
tool_config.learning_objective: Students group everyday objects that look alike and notice which ones roll, slide or stand.
tool_config.screen: A bright table seen from the front. The five toys from the story stand on it, large and shaded. They are a football, a die, a shoebox, a bottle and a birthday cap. A tray under the table holds five look-alike partners. They are a marble, a cube-shaped box, an eraser, a chalk stick and a wooden cone. These object names are for the builder only. Every toy and every partner is shown as an UNLABELLED picture tile: no word is written on or under any tile, so no solid name reaches the child. No shape name is written anywhere. Only the words rolls, slides and stands appear, after a push or a try. A push shows what the object does the way it lies now. A football or a marble rolls every way. A bottle or a chalk stick lying down rolls one way. A cap or a wooden cone lying down rolls round and round. A die, a cube-shaped box, a shoebox and an eraser slide. Any object standing upright just slides when nudged.
controls: Drag a partner next to its toy
tool_config.instruction: Turn, push and stand each toy. Put the ones that look alike together.
feedback: Alike pair: the partner glows beside its toy. Push both and they move the same way.
Not alike: the partner slides back to the tray. Turn both and look at every side again.
Push result: rolls every way, rolls one way, rolls round and round, or slides.
Stand result is one of these. Stands on a flat side. Stands on a flat end. Stands on its round base. Will not stand.

content.text:
1. Predict first: how many flat sides does a die have?
2. A die has 6 flat sides. Each flat side is a face.
3. Where two faces meet is a line. The line is an edge.
4. A pointed place on a solid is a corner.
5. A football has one curved face. It has no edges and no corners.
6. A face can be flat or curved.

content.text:
Worked example: How many faces, edges and corners does a shoebox have?
1. The top is 1 face. The bottom is 1 face. The 4 sides are 4 faces.
2. 1 + 1 + 4 = 6 faces.
3. 4 edges go round the top. 4 edges go round the bottom. 4 edges go up the sides.
4. 4 + 4 + 4 = 12 edges.
5. 4 corners are on the top. 4 corners are on the bottom.
6. 4 + 4 = 8 corners.
Answer: Example: a shoebox has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 corners.

media.teaching_notes: Jaya, Devika, the children in two tables in the craft corner, with a cardboard screen standing between them. For the toy show, Jaya builds a little house on her table. visual_key.cuboid: a solid box with six rectangle faces, drawn long and flat or tall; the book's chart colour is yellow; the clean real example is a shoebox (key shoebox)
visual_key.cylinder: a solid with two flat round ends and one curved side, drawn with a thin ellipse on top; the book's chart colour is lime green; the clean real example is a plain bottle (key bottle)
visual_key.cone: a solid with one flat round base, one curved side and a pointed tip; the book's chart colour is lavender purple; the clean real example is a birthday cap (key birthday_cap)
visual_key.sphere: a proper shaded 3D ball in every picture, video and tool: round from every side, with a soft highlight and a shadow, never a flat disc; the book's chart colour is red; the book draws its sphere as a flat disc (the chart, Q2, Q6) and as a flat round part on two shop toys, and this plan does not copy those discs; the clean real example is a football (key football)
visual_key.football: a real round football (a soccer ball, not an oval one) with black and white patches, shown as a full round solid with light and shadow; it rolls in every direction and has no flat part to stand on; the clean real example of a sphere, never drawn as a flat disc
visual_key.birthday_cap: a plain paper birthday cap standing upright: a pointed tip, one curved side and a round rim at the bottom, in one bright colour with simple stripes or dots, with no pom-pom on the tip and no strap that changes the outline; the clean real example of a cone (the hollow underside is never shown, CLASH 27); on its side it rolls round and round, upright it stands on its flat round base
visual_key.shoebox: a closed shoebox with its lid on: six flat rectangle faces and square corners, one plain colour, with no handle, no cut-out and no rounded corners; the clean real example of a cuboid; it slides and it stands on any of its flat faces and does not roll
visual_key.bottle: a plain cylindrical bottle: straight sides, a flat round bottom and a flat round lid, with no narrow neck, no waist and no ridges, so the shape is not misrepresented; the clean real example of a cylinder; on its side it rolls one way only, upright it stands on its flat bottom or its flat lid
visual_key.marble: a small glass marble: a shaded 3D ball with a soft highlight and a thin colour swirl inside, round from every side, never a flat disc; a second clean real example of a sphere; it rolls in every direction and has no flat part to stand on
visual_key.cube_box: a closed cube-shaped box with its lid on: six equal square faces and square corners, one plain colour, with no ribbon, no handle and no rounded corners; a second clean real example of a cube; it slides and stands on any of its six flat faces and does not roll
visual_key.eraser: a plain white rubber eraser: a closed block with six flat rectangle faces and square corners, no sleeve and no rounded corners; a second clean real example of a cuboid; it slides and stands on any flat face and does not roll
visual_key.book: a closed plain hard-cover book lying flat: six flat rectangle faces, square corners, one plain colour and no picture or writing on it; a third clean real example of a cuboid; it slides and stands on any flat face and does not roll
visual_key.chalk: a plain white stick of chalk: straight sides and two flat round ends, no taper; a second clean real example of a cylinder; lying down it rolls one way only, upright it stands on a flat end
visual_key.wooden_cone: a solid wooden toy cone: a pointed tip, one curved side and one flat round base, in one natural wood colour; a second clean real example of a cone; on its side it rolls round and round, upright it stands on its flat round base
visual_key.table: a plain classroom table drawn whole and upright: one flat cuboid top on four straight cuboid legs, one plain colour; a real object made of more than one solid, used only in the Tool 4 question about things made of more than one shape
visual_key.simple_house: the plan's own simple house for Tool 3: a yellow cuboid for the walls with a lavender cone for the roof, drawn like the cuboid and cone keys, with no windows or door; seen first small from far away and then close up; it is not Jaya's two-storey house and not one of Jaya's other houses
visual_key.flat_circle: a flat circle drawn on paper or cut out of paper: one flat face and no thickness; shown only beside a real ball in the T7 photo as a clearly secondary pair; it is never a solid shape, never used for a sphere and not part of any objective or tool (CLASH 2)
visual_key.face_edge_corner_figure: the book's cube picture with three arrows labelled face, edge and corner
visual_key.craft_faces: animal and bird faces drawn on old boxes and bottles: a puppy on a bottle (cylinder), a cat on a cuboid, a pig on a box (cube), a bird with a pointed beak on a cone
visual_key.jaya_rocket: from the top: a pink cone, a lavender cube, a cyan cube, a large orange cylinder; yellow, green, red and light blue cuboids stand around its foot
visual_key.devika_toy_engine: a pink-red cylinder, two small yellow cones as chimneys, a light blue cab with a window, a grey-blue base slab, black wheels and a pull string
visual_key.shop_toys: four toys: an orange animal from a cone and a cylinder, a red shaded ball on a grey stick, a yellow cat with a cylinder body and a shaded ball head, a wooden board with cubes and cuboids; the round parts are shaded balls, not the flat discs the book draws (CLASH 16)
visual_key.jaya_houses: four models: a pink cone on a green cylinder, a yellow cone on a teal cube, two pink cones on a wooden board, a two-storey teal house with arched windows, yellow cones and white cylinder pillars
visual_key.boy_tower: a lavender cuboid slab, a yellow and green banded cylinder and a cyan cone on top, on a wooden board
visual_key.clay_and_sticks: beige clay balls (each a small shaded ball) joined by thin green and white striped sticks, making a cuboid frame and a four-ball shape
visual_key.cube_shapes: joined cubes: a green three-armed shape, a pink plus-like shape, three teal cubes in a row, and, for ch2.say2, the plan's own stack of 10 coloured cubes in one row, standing in four columns of 4, 3, 2 and 1 cubes like steps (4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10), so every cube can be seen or counted by turning it (no cube behind another; it replaces the book's stepped stack, CLASH 28)
visual_key.die: a cube with 1 to 6 dots: the plan always draws a plain white die with black dots, square corners and exact dot counts (never a wrong count), in the T8 picture, in Tool 8 and in the game, so they match (the book's pink die of Q7, which shows only 6, 5 and 3, is not copied); the clean real example of a cube; it slides and stands on any of its six flat faces and tips over instead of rolling smoothly
visual_key.stacked_models: flat orange, pink, green, red and yellow cuboids stacked or offset to make four models, and two orange boards with brown cylinders and cyan cones
visual_key.game_border: a green textured frame with white picture squares of everyday objects, Start at the top left and Finish at the end; the plan's own board has 24 picture squares and uses only clean examples of the five solids, not the book's clay pot, watermelon, cake slice or roti stack (CLASH 26). In order: 1 birthday cap, 2 shoebox, 3 football, 4 die, 5 bottle, 6 book, 7 wooden cone, 8 marble, 9 eraser, 10 cube box, 11 chalk, 12 football, 13 shoebox, 14 birthday cap, 15 die, 16 bottle, 17 book, 18 marble, 19 wooden cone, 20 cube box, 21 eraser, 22 chalk, 23 football, 24 die. So cone 4 squares, cuboid 6, sphere 5, cube 5, cylinder 4 (24 in all). Some pictures show the object turned or lying down. The key under the board is the book's: 1 dot cylinder, 2 dots sphere, 3 dots cone, 4 dots cube, 5 dots cuboid, 6 dots move 2 steps forward

story.thread: Children make toys and models from solid shapes: they draw faces on boxes, bottles and a cone, Jaya builds a rocket and houses, Devika buys a toy engine, and friends build and describe models together.
story.setting: a craft corner with old boxes, bottles and cans; a toy shop; a classroom
